description: M12 phase B speed-envelope gates for the M10 balance controller. Commands are piecewise-linear knots [t_s, velocity_m_s, yaw_rate_rad_s] (linear between knots), or replays of the phase A ideal-follower commands. Every case runs on the C core with the sensor model, a free base, finite motor limits and physical contact. The envelope itself is config/robot.json m10.targets.drive_envelope.
status: Criteria signed off by the user on 21 October 2026 at the phase B exit

criteria.basis: Physical failure stays the acceptance limit (20 deg pitch, 10 deg roll, forbidden contact, joint limits, saturation at most 0.5 s). Gated cases also keep 5 deg of pitch margin to it. Speed overshoot above the largest command at most 0.15 m/s, an absolute bound because the overshoot comes from the lean transient of a start and is about 0.1 m/s from 0.3 to 1.2 m/s (the recorded M10 acceptance drive overshoots 0.3 m/s by 0.13 m/s); 0.15 m/s for the half second of the transient is under 0.08 m of range. Plateau speed error at most 0.05 m/s (4 % of 1.2 m/s; the 0.3 m/s acceptance allows 0.03 m/s, 10 %). Yaw-rate error and final heading error are the acceptance turn limits. A stop may run past the stopping distance of the shaped reference by at most 0.15 m: the loss rule (following-m12.json loss) brings the robot to rest 0.8 m after the last detection from 1.0 m/s, so 0.15 m keeps the robot 0.05 m short of the 1.0 m nominal range. In a replay the robot's path stays within 0.2 m of the ideal follower's path, inside the 0.3 m between the nominal range and the lower edge of the range band. A case recovers when the last 2 s have pitch within 2 deg and speed within 0.03 m/s (the acceptance recovery rule). A slope case holds instead when the last 2 s have speed within 0.03 m/s: on a slope the held pitch includes the slope lean, so the M10 suite judges slopes by survival and rollback, not by the pitch recovery rule.

drive_step.purpose: Step to the 1.2 m/s envelope speed and a step stop; the controller's shaping sets the profile

drive_ramp.purpose: Follower-like ramp at 1.25 m/s^2 to 1.2 m/s and a 1.0 m/s^2 brake

spin.purpose: Spin at the 1.0 rad/s envelope yaw rate both ways, at rest

arc_r2.purpose: 2 m radius at 1.0 m/s (0.5 m/s^2 lateral, the target curve limit)

arc_r1.purpose: 1 m radius at 0.7 m/s (0.5 m/s^2 lateral)

weave.purpose: Alternating turns at 0.8 rad/s while driving at 1.0 m/s, reversing the yaw rate at the yaw acceleration limit

push_fast_+2.purpose: 2 N s forward push at 4 s while driving at 1.2 m/s

push_fast_-2.purpose: 2 N s backward push at 4 s while driving at 1.2 m/s

slopes.basis: Up and down the M10 acceptance slopes at 1.0 m/s, driving forward (downhill is a negative ground slope); the robot must survive, stop and hold

replays.basis: The ideal follower's speed and yaw rate (artifacts/m12/requirements/follower_traces.npz) as the balance controller's commands, zero while the follower waits or holds

variants.basis: The M10 acceptance variants. A wheel lag is applied to physics.hub_motor.FOC_time_constant_s, the constant the M10 hub drives use (the inherited acceptance job sets motor.torque_time_constant, which the M10 drives do not read, so on M10 it never applied). The modelled moteus FOC lag is 0.8 ms; 10 ms is added as the largest lag both the pre-phase-B and the phase B controllers survive in the 0.3 m/s acceptance cases (artifacts/m12/speed/lag_check).

recorded_shortfalls.status: Accepted by the user at the phase B sign-off, 21 October 2026
recorded_shortfalls.basis: Wheel lag: a real 25 ms hub torque lag also fails the 0.3 m/s M10 acceptance drive and combined cases with the controller before phase B (artifacts/m12/speed/lag_check/before_phase_b.json), so this is an inherited M10 gap, hidden because the inherited variant did not apply on M10; it is not a phase B regression. The phase B controller survives a 10 ms lag at speed. slope_up_4 and slope_up_8: after the stop the robot creeps back to its hold point, peaking at 0.041 and 0.032 m/s in the last 2 s (0.016 and 0.009 m/s at the end), over the 0.03 m/s hold speed proposed here; the M10 suite judges slope holds by rollback (at most 0.1 m; these cases roll back 0.029 and 0.042 m as they first settle on the slope), which they meet. slope_up_8 passed (0.024 m/s) while the estimator's acceleration compensation also ran during the hold; it is now off while holding, so a push at rest is not taken for a drive acceleration (artifacts/m12/speed/regression/push_low.json). The hold keeps its pre-phase-B rate limit (controller_m10.json hold_command_acceleration); shaping the hold reference with the lean feedforward held this case to 0.029 m/s but lost the push recovery at rest under a 25 ms hub lag (artifacts/m12/speed/lag_check/attribution.json).
